subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support a Docker sandbox `no-new-privileges` opt-out or fallback for hosts where the flag causes exec EPERM?
rationale: The source-reproducible failure blocks sandbox sessions, but disabling or retrying without this flag changes the sandbox hardening boundary and adds config/fallback behavior that repository policy reserves for maintainer security/product judgment.

options.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
options.body: Add a documented dangerous config key, default it to the current secure behavior, and surface the weakened runtime in status/doctor/security audit output.

options.title: Diagnostic Only
options.body: Keep the flag mandatory and improve startup/status errors so operators can identify the host-level Docker incompatibility without guessing from container logs.

options.title: Narrow EPERM Fallback
options.body: Retry without the flag only for a tightly detected startup EPERM and record the runtime as weakened for audit/status visibility.

recommendation.title: Explicit Dangerous Override
recommendation.body: Add a documented dangerous config key, default it to the current secure behavior, and surface the weakened runtime in status/doctor/security audit output.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current Docker sandbox module containing this hardening flag and has the strongest nearby sandbox history signal.
